chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who buys a slave who is running away (abiq) from his family, so he said: 'It is not valid unless he buys something else with him, so he says: I buy from you this item and your slave for such and such an amount. If he is unable to capture the slave, the price he paid is considered spent on the item.'

key_terms.آبِق: A slave who has run away or is absent from his owner

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for buying a slave who has run away from his owner?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines a specific legal mechanism (*hiyal*) to mitigate the risk of purchasing a fugitive slave (*abiq*) by bundling the transaction with another commodity. In Shia jurisprudence, this ensures that if the slave escapes and cannot be reclaimed, the buyer does not suffer a total loss, as the paid price is considered spent on the accompanying item, thereby preserving the validity of the sale.
